zh.question: 细胞有哪些共同结构，又怎样用不同形状完成不同的工作？
zh.observe: 沿结构、物质与能量、分工三条观察线，先找到同一细胞的膜与内部，再比较呼吸和光合作用，最后观察皮肤、肌肉、神经、运氧、防御与止血。每个实验保留自己的进度，切换样本不表示细胞变身。

academic.title: 边界与内部空间各有作用
academic.body: 细胞膜分隔内外并参与物质交换；植物细胞壁位于膜外，提供机械支持，不能把壁和膜当作同一层。叶肉细胞的大液泡有自己的膜，中央液泡占据较大体积，细胞质和细胞器多分布在周边。线粒体的内膜向内折叠；叶绿体则在包膜内具有类囊体膜系统。画面突出层次，未按真实厚度、数量与拥挤程度绘制。

academic.title: 有遗传信息，不一定有细胞核
academic.body: 典型动植物细胞的大部分 DNA 在有膜包围的细胞核中；线粒体及叶绿体还有少量自身 DNA。细菌没有这样的细胞核，主要 DNA 位于拟核区域，但细菌仍是细胞，能交换物质并进行代谢。细胞会因分化而特化，例如成熟哺乳动物红细胞没有细胞核和线粒体；代表性结构图不能作为每个细胞的通用清单。 皮肤的层状屏障依靠许多细胞；骨骼肌纤维通常有多个细胞核，收缩时细丝相对滑动而不是细丝缩短。神经信号沿膜传播，化学突触另以递质传递。人的血小板是细胞片段，止血还需要血浆蛋白。运氧、防御、止血是不同过程，不是同一段血液必经的三步。

academic.title: 制造糖与利用营养物质可以并行
academic.body: 有氧呼吸从糖等营养物质中释放能量，并使其中一部分成为 ATP 等可利用的化学形式，另有能量转为热。糖的分解先在细胞质进行，线粒体参与后续过程。叶肉细胞利用光能，以二氧化碳和水参与制造糖并释放氧；糖的碳来自二氧化碳，释放的氧来自水。植物也进行呼吸，白天和夜间都可以；分开播放只为比较，并不表示光合作用与呼吸只能轮流发生。

zh.misconception: 植物不只在夜里呼吸，也不是所有植物细胞都能光合作用。细菌没有细胞核和线粒体，却有 DNA，也会进行能量转换。
zh.boundary: 这是配色和放大的结构、物质变化示意，不是显微照片。不同细胞与膜厚不按同一尺度；箭头概括多步反应，不是固定管道，小点不代表真实分子比例。金色 ATP 是携带可用能量的分子的符号，绿圆点表示氨基酸，连串表示蛋白质链；ATP 并不变成这些原料。该例只引入能量与合成的关系，未展开核糖体、RNA、氨基酸活化及 GTP 等步骤。不模拟 ATP 产量、净气体交换或无氧代谢，也不把这两种过程套给所有细菌。 分工图保留各自的代表样本与简化：中性粒细胞不代表全部白细胞；人的成熟红细胞不能套用典型有核细胞的线粒体示例。六种工作彼此独立，不建立未经模拟的统一生理时间线。

narration.label: 边界里面有什么
narration.text: 把世界看得小一点，再小一点。我们的身体、叶子，还有细菌，都和细胞有关。先选动物细胞，找一找最外面的细胞膜。它把里面和外面分开，也参与调节物质来去。点一个结构，下面的窗口就会靠近同一个地方。图里的颜色是帮我们分辨的，不是肉眼看到的颜色。
narration.cue: 选动物细胞，依次点细胞膜和细胞核，指向整体虚线框及对应局部窗口。

narration.label: 小细菌也有信息
narration.text: 再找找 DNA，它保存着遗传信息。动物和叶肉细胞里，大部分 DNA 在细胞核中。换成细菌，停一停：没有那个细胞核，DNA 就不见了吗？看，它还在里面！细菌自己就是一个细胞。叶肉细胞还有大大的液泡，绿色的叶绿体和许多结构分布在旁边。
narration.cue: 选 DNA 后切换三种细胞，留出观察停顿；在细菌中选细胞核核对缺失提示，再看叶肉液泡。

narration.label: 动物细胞怎样得到能量
narration.text: 细胞不只是装着东西，它也在做事情。慢慢拖进度，跟着金色的糖看一看。糖先在细胞质里分解，分解后的小块继续往前走。看，它们和氧都来到圈出的线粒体附近，参与后面的一连串变化。这里会形成二氧化碳和水，还把糖里的一部分能量转到一种叫 ATP 的分子上。跟着金色标记，它代表 ATP。再看看绿圆点，每一个表示一种叫氨基酸的小原料。细胞把这些原料连接起来，形成蛋白质链。ATP 为这个制造过程中的一些步骤提供能量，可不是变成了绿圆点。能量没有凭空出现，而是换成了细胞更容易使用的形式。
narration.cue: 选动物细胞与线粒体，缓慢拖动进度：22% 至 32% 看糖分解，32% 至 52% 跟随小块和氧，52% 至 70% 看 ATP 形成，70% 至结束看能量输送与材料连接。图示符号不是分子形状或数量。

narration.label: 从叶肉细胞到身体分工
narration.text: 现在看看叶肉细胞。选用光制造糖：光带来能量，水和二氧化碳参与形成糖，还会释放氧。糖可以留下，也可以供植物别的部分使用。再选利用营养物质，原来植物也会从糖里得到可用能量！白天和夜晚都可以。我们把两件事分开看，不表示它们一定要排队轮流做。 再看看身体里的不同细胞：皮肤连成保护层，肌肉中的细丝相对滑动，神经元传递信息，红细胞运送氧气。它们不是同一颗细胞变来变去，而是形状和结构适合不同工作。血小板则是大细胞形成的小片段，和血浆蛋白一起帮助止血。
narration.cue: 选叶肉细胞和叶绿体，观看光合作用；随后选择线粒体与利用营养物质，对照两种过程。 随后进入分工，逐个比较不同样本；保留它们的独立进度。

en.question: What do cells share, and how do different shapes support different jobs?
en.observe: Explore structure, matter and energy, then specialisation: locate a cell's boundary and interior, compare respiration and photosynthesis, and observe skin, muscle, neurons, oxygen transport, defence and clotting. Each experiment retains its progress; changing specimens does not mean a cell transforms.

academic.title: Boundaries and internal spaces have different roles
academic.body: The cell membrane separates inside from outside and regulates exchange. A plant cell wall lies outside it and provides mechanical support. The large leaf-cell vacuole has its own membrane and occupies much of the interior, with cytoplasm and organelles around it. Mitochondrial inner membranes fold inward, while chloroplasts contain a distinct thylakoid membrane system. Thickness, number and crowding are simplified.

academic.title: Genetic information does not require a nucleus
academic.body: Most DNA in typical animal and plant cells is enclosed in a nucleus; mitochondria and chloroplasts also contain some DNA. Bacteria lack a nucleus but have DNA in a nucleoid region and carry out metabolism. Specialisation changes cell structures: mature mammalian red cells lack both a nucleus and mitochondria. A representative diagram is not a universal checklist. Skin barriers involve many cells. Skeletal muscle fibres usually have multiple nuclei, and contraction involves relative filament sliding, not shorter filaments. Neural signals propagate along membranes, with chemical transmitters crossing the illustrated synapse. Human platelets are cell fragments; clotting also uses plasma proteins. Oxygen transport, defence and clotting are different processes, not three mandatory steps for the same blood parcel.

academic.title: Making sugars and using nutrients can overlap
academic.body: Aerobic respiration releases energy from nutrients, capturing some in usable chemical forms such as ATP and releasing some as heat. Sugar breakdown begins in the cytoplasm, with mitochondria involved in later steps. Leaf cells use light energy to make sugars using carbon dioxide and water. Sugar carbon comes from carbon dioxide; released oxygen comes from water. Plants respire in both day and night. Separate playback does not mean photosynthesis and respiration must take turns.

en.misconception: Plants respire during the day as well as at night, and not every plant cell photosynthesizes. Bacteria have DNA and convert energy despite lacking nuclei and mitochondria.
en.boundary: These coloured, enlarged structures and pathways are not micrographs. Cells and membrane thicknesses do not share a common scale. Paths summarize multiple reactions rather than fixed pipes, and markers are not molecular ratios. Gold ATP is a symbol for molecules carrying usable energy. Green dots represent amino acids and a joined string represents a protein chain; ATP does not turn into these materials. This example only introduces energy support for synthesis, omitting ribosomes, RNA, amino acid activation and GTP-dependent steps. ATP yields, net gas exchange and anaerobic pathways are not modelled, and the two examples do not describe all bacteria. Specialisation views retain their own specimens and limitations: neutrophils do not represent every white cell, and the mitochondrial example of a typical nucleated cell cannot be imposed on mature human red cells. The six jobs are independent, not one simulated physiological timeline.

narration.label: What lies inside the boundary?
narration.text: Let us look at a smaller world. Our bodies, leaves and bacteria all have something to do with cells. Choose the animal cell and find its outer cell membrane. It separates inside from outside and helps regulate what enters and leaves. Choose a structure and the lower window moves closer to that same place. The colours help us tell structures apart; they are not what our eyes would normally see.
narration.cue: Choose the animal cell, then membrane and nucleus. Match the dashed whole-cell frame to the close-up.

narration.label: Tiny bacteria have information too
narration.text: Find DNA, which stores inherited information. In animal and leaf cells, most DNA is in the nucleus. Switch to a bacterium and pause. If that nucleus is missing, has the DNA vanished? No, it is still inside! A bacterium is itself a cell. The leaf cell also has a large vacuole, with green chloroplasts and other structures around it.
narration.cue: Keep DNA selected across all three cells and pause. Select the bacterial nucleus to check the absence message, then inspect the leaf vacuole.

narration.label: How an animal cell gets energy
narration.text: A cell does more than hold things. Slowly move the progress control and follow the gold sugar. It first breaks down in the cytoplasm, and the smaller pieces keep moving. They and oxygen reach the circled mitochondrial region and take part in further reactions. Carbon dioxide and water form, and some energy from the sugar is captured in molecules called ATP. Follow the gold symbol, which represents ATP. Look at the green dots: each represents a small building block called an amino acid. The cell joins these building blocks into a protein chain. ATP supplies energy for some steps of this process; it does not turn into green dots. The energy did not appear from nowhere: it changed into a form the cell can use more easily.
narration.cue: Choose the animal cell and mitochondrion. Scrub through sugar breakdown at 22–32%, follow the pieces and oxygen at 32–52%, ATP formation at 52–70%, then energy delivery and assembly through the end. Symbols are not molecular shapes or counts.

narration.label: From leaf cells to specialised jobs
narration.text: Now look at the leaf cell. Choose Making sugars with light. Light supplies energy; water and carbon dioxide help form sugars, and oxygen is released. Sugars can stay or supply other parts of the plant. Choose Using nutrients next. Plants also gain usable energy from sugars, during both day and night! We show these processes separately to look closely, although they do not have to wait their turn. Now compare jobs in the body: skin forms a barrier, muscle filaments slide, neurons carry signals and red cells transport oxygen. These are different cells, with shapes and structures suited to their jobs, not one cell transforming. Platelets are fragments made by large cells; they work with plasma proteins to help stop bleeding.
narration.cue: Choose the leaf cell and chloroplasts to watch photosynthesis. Then select the mitochondrion and Using nutrients to compare. Then compare distinct specimens in the specialisation view, retaining their independent progress.
